subject: maths
question: A bicycle is sold for {₹}1800 at a loss of 10\%. At what price should it be sold to gain 15\%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of **10%** implies that the **Selling Price** is **90%** of the **Cost Price**.

Desired gain of **15%** implies that the new **Selling Price** should be **115%** of the **Cost Price**.

Given: 90% → ₹1800

Therefore: 115% → (1800 ÷ 90) × 115 = 20 × 115 = ₹2300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First Selling Price (SP₁) = **₹1800**

Loss Percentage (L%) = **10%**

Desired Profit Percentage (P%) = **15%**

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]

New Selling Price (SP₂) = [CP × (100 + Profit%)] ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61a003dc2032667930624188ca16d25a21742ae2fb568607450b799bab10f27e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (1800 × 100) ÷ (100 − 10)

⇒ CP = (1800 × 100) ÷ 90

⇒ CP = 20 × 100 = **₹2000**

⇒ SP₂ = [2000 × (100 + 15)] ÷ 100

⇒ SP₂ = [2000 × 115] ÷ 100

⇒ SP₂ = 20 × 115 = **₹2300**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise.

Relationship between SP and CP

SP = CP × (100 ± Change%) ÷ 100. Use (+) for **Profit** and (−) for **Loss**.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) − Discount. Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.
